headline: A hot September PPI and a deepening global chip sell-off (KOSPI −7.6%) have Nasdaq-100 futures down 1.3% while Dow futures edge up; Ericsson jumps 12% on results, Penske Automotive 8% on a $212-a-share take-private, and ManpowerGroup falls 15%.

Yahoo's VIX change is shown as quoted (+0.66); its 'previous close' field (15.27) looked stale, so % is Yahoo's own figure.
drivers: The AI and semiconductor sell-off that followed Wednesday's hot CPI deepened overnight: South Korea's KOSPI fell about 7.6% (SK hynix −11%, Samsung −9% locally), the Nikkei about 5% and Taiwan's Taiex about 3%. Reports on Anthropic's revenue and profitability, plus concern over CoreWeave's borrowing costs and record Oracle default-insurance prices, added to worries about AI spending and financing. September PPI came in far hotter than expected: +1.3% month over month (est. 0.5%) and 6.3% year over year (est. ~5.3–5.5%), with core +0.7% m/m. Retail sales rose 0.8% (est. 0.3%) but the control group only 0.1%, claims were steady at 199K, the Empire State index jumped to 25.5 and Philly Fed slipped to 20.9. Futures split after the data: Nasdaq-100 −1.3% and S&P 500 −0.3%, while the Dow is +0.4% and the Russell 2000 is flat. The 10-year yield eased to 5.10% and the dollar slipped. Analysts quoted by TheStreet see a Fed hike as roughly a coin flip at the meeting in two weeks. TSMC beat and guided Q4 revenue to $52.3–54.3B, but its ADR trades −3.3% with the chip group (SOXX −3.0%). Brent fell below $105 on possible U.S. easing of sanctions on Russia's tanker fleet. Gold is up 1.6%, and Bitcoin is down 2.3% near $80.7K.
